gaps.lead: She prefers reading books to watching television.
gaps.explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

gaps.lead: We wanted to continue our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
gaps.sentence: We ___ on with our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
gaps.hint: unfulfilled wish: would have liked to
gaps.explanation: An unrealised wish about the past: 'would have liked to carry on'.

gaps.lead: Pay claims must be submitted before the end of the month.
gaps.sentence: You have ___ your pay claims before the end of the month.
gaps.explanation: 'Must be submitted' becomes 'you have to put in your claims'.

gaps.lead: I only understood the pattern much later.
gaps.explanation: Front 'only + time phrase' forces inversion: Only much later did I understand.

gaps.lead: 'I broke the window,' the boy said.
gaps.sentence: When caught, the boy ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: admit + -ing, or admit having + past participle for the earlier action.

gaps.lead: The soup needed a little more salt.
gaps.explanation: needed a little more = didn't have enough (salt).
